questions.q: How do I register to vote?
questions.a: You can register online (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/ovrweb/govoteky/), or by submitting a voter registration card by mail or in-person.

questions.q: How do I check if I am registered to vote?
questions.a: You can verify your voter registration online at govote.ky.gov (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/ovrweb/govoteky).

questions.q: Do I have to register before each election?
questions.a: No, once you have registered to vote, you do not have to re-register for each election. Re-registration is necessary only if you have moved or legally changed your name.

questions.q: I recently moved, do I have to update my registration?
questions.a: Yes, updating your registration is necessary if you have moved or legally changed your name. You can make updates to your registration online, or by submitting a voter registration application by mail or in-person.

questions.q: The deadline to register has passed, can I still update my registration?
questions.a: No, once the voter registration deadline has passed, the voter registration rolls are frozen until after the next election.

questions.q: I am a U.S. Citizen residing overseas, how do I register to vote?
questions.a: For information on how to register or obtain a ballot, visit Military and Overseas Voters (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Military-or-Overseas-Voters.aspx).

questions.q: I am in the military, how can I request a ballot?
questions.a: For information on how to obtain an absentee ballot, visit Military and Overseas Voters (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Military-or-Overseas-Voters.aspx).

questions.q: I am disabled, how can I request a ballot?
questions.a: If you have a disability that prevents you from marking a paper ballot and you would like to request an accessible absentee ballot via the state's accessible absentee portal, please contact your county clerk (https://elect.ky.gov/About-Us/Pages/County-Clerks.aspx).

questions.q: How do I cancel my voter registration?
questions.a: To cancel your voter registration, contact the KY State Board of Elections (https://elect.ky.gov/About-Us/Pages/Contact-Us.aspx).

questions.q: I am 17 years old, can I register to vote?
questions.a: State law allows for pre-registration at 17 years of age, but you must be 18 years of age on or before the next General Election Day to vote. If you are 17 and will be 18 on the next General Election, you may vote in the Primary Election.

questions.q: How many people are registered to vote in Kentucky?
questions.a:
The State Board of Elections runs registration reports every month. Review this year's registration reports here (https://elect.ky.gov/Resources/Pages/Registration-Statistics.aspx).

questions.q: How do I get voter registration cards for my registration drive?
questions.a:
· Remember you can always encourage citizens to use their smartphone to visit govote.ky.gov (https://govote.ky.gov/) to register online.

· Request cards from your local County Clerk. The individual or group hosting the drive must act under the supervision and directions of the County Clerk and must return these completed forms to the County Clerk for official registration by the County Clerk.

· For a substantial number of cards contact the State Board of Elections.

· You may also direct voters to our website (elect.ky.gov (http://www.elect.ky.gov/)) to print out the online Voter Registration Card (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Documents/SBE%2001%20-%20KY%20Voter%20Registration%20Application%20FILLABLE%20406.pdf)

questions.q: Is the person eligible to register to vote in Kentucky?
How will a person know if they are registered to vote?
questions.a: · The person will receive a confirmation card in the mail from the County Clerk with the voter's precinct name and voting location address.

questions.q: Is the voter registration card complete?
questions.a:
· A complete residential address must be provided on the voter registration card. Failure to do so will result in a delay in the processing of the application because the County Clerk may not be able to assign a precinct.

· A mailing address must be provided ONLY if it is different from the residential address. The mailing address is used to send the voter a confirmation that his/her voter registration has been processed or when the County Clerk's office needs more information in order to process the registration application.

· The voter must mark a choice in the party registration field. If no party registration is selected, the voter is eligible to vote for only nonpartisan offices in any primary election.

· A date of birth is required to verify that the voter meets the minimum age requirement for voting.

· Two witnesses are required for a voter signature ONLY if the voter uses a “mark" to sign his or her name.

· See KRS 116.155 (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=27330).

questions.q: If the voter is already registered, how does the voter change his/her political party registration?
questions.a:
· If a voter is already registered, the voter may change his/her political party registration at any time, but must change prior to December 31 to be eligible to vote in their new party's primary election.

· See KRS 116.055 (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=48900).

questions.q: The voter has moved. What does he need to do?
questions.a: · It is very important that the County Clerk have the most up-to-date information as possible. A voter with a name or address change should complete a new voter registration card with the updated information and current signature or update their registration at govote.ky.gov (https://govote.ky.gov/).

questions.q: Where is the completed voter registration card sent?
questions.a: · The voter registration card should be routed to the clerk in the county listed on the voter registration card [County where you live], NOT to the State Board of Elections. Find a listing of County Clerks here (https://elect.ky.gov/About-Us/Pages/County-Clerks.aspx) or contact the State Board of Elections.

questions.q: How will the voter know where to vote?
questions.a:
· The voter will receive a notice in the mail from the County Clerk with his/her precinct name and voting location address. The polls are open from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., local time. All voters in line by 6 p.m. will be able to vote. If a voter has any questions concerning where to vote, he/she may call the County Clerk or visit the Voter Information Center (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/vic/) available on the State Board of Elections website. The Voter Information Center includes the address of the voter's precinct, a map with driving directions and party affiliation.

Penalties

KRS 119.025 (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=27723): No person may be registered to vote in more than one precinct or in a precinct where he is not a legal voter or gives false information when registering to vote.
 Class D Felony

KRS 119.035 (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=27725): No person may fraudulently or unlawfully alter any registration record.
 Class D Felony

KRS 119.045 (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=27727): No person may forcibly prevent another person from registering or interfere with the duties of a registration officer.
 Class A misdemeanor

KRS 119.207 (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=27763): No person may compensate another person for registering voters based upon the total number of voters a person registers or the total number of voters a person registers for a particular party.
 Class B misdemeanor

questions.q: Where is my polling place?
questions.a: You can find your polling place at www.govote.ky.gov (http://www.govote.ky.gov/)

questions.q: Am I entitled to time off for voting on Election Day?
questions.a:
If you are working on Election Day, you may be entitled to a maximum of four consecutive hours off from work in order to vote or cast an absentee ballot if you make a request for time off with your employer.

Your employer may specify the hours you may take leave to cast a ballot.

questions.q: What identification can I bring to the polling place?
questions.a: All voters must produce identification at the polling place. Further information regarding valid forms of ID may be found at: Voter ID Requirements (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Absentee-Excused-In-Person.aspx)

questions.q: What time are the polls open on Election Day?
questions.a: Polls are open from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM local time on Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026. If you are in line at 6:00 PM, you will be allowed to vote.

questions.q: What time are the polls open on the days prior to Election Day?
questions.a:
Time polls are open during excused, in-person absentee and no-excuse in-person absentee is found on www.govote.ky.gov (http://www.govote.ky.gov/) or contact your County Clerk's office (https://elect.ky.gov/About-Us/Pages/County-Clerks.aspx).

Q: I registered to vote, but I did not receive a confirmation card.

A: Contact your County Clerk's office (https://elect.ky.gov/About-Us/Pages/County-Clerks.aspx) to find out the status of your address confirmation.

questions.q: Do I have to vote according to party affiliation?
questions.a: Kentucky conducts political party primaries before each General Election. In Primary Elections, voters may only vote for candidates of their same political affiliation and non-partisan candidates. In General Elections, voters may choose to vote for candidates of any party.

questions.q: How do I switch political parties?
questions.a: You can change your political party at www.govote.ky.gov (http://www.govote.ky.gov/) or by submitting an updated registration application to your county clerk. You must change your party affiliation by December 31 for eligibility to vote in the Primary Election the following year.

questions.q: I will be out of town on Election Day. How can I vote?
questions.a:
You can request an absentee ballot by mail at www.govote.ky.gov (http://www.govote.ky.gov/) Saturday, September 19, 2026 - October 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM, excused in-person Wednesday – Friday, October 21 - October 23, 2026 and Monday – Wednesday, October 29 - October 31, 2026, or no excuse, in-person absentee on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, October 29 - October 31, 2026.

questions.q: Who are UOCAVA voters in Kentucky?
questions.a:
- Members of the United States Uniformed Services and the merchant marines, active or reserve members, including activated status National Guard, and their family members
- Kentucky citizens residing outside of the United States
- An overseas voter who, before leaving the United States, was last eligible to vote in the Commonwealth of Kentucky and, except for his or her absence from the state, otherwise satisfies the Commonwealth of Kentucky's voter eligibility requirements;
- An overseas voter who, before leaving the United States, would have been last eligible to vote in the Commonwealth of Kentucky had the voter then been of voting age and, except for his or her absence from the state, otherwise satisfies the Commonwealth of Kentucky's voter eligibility requirements; or
- An overseas voter who was born outside the United States, is not described in paragraph (c) or (d) of this subsection, and, except for his or her absence from the state, otherwise satisfies the Commonwealth of Kentucky's voter eligibility requirements, if:

   1. The last place where a parent or legal guardian of the voter was, or under this chapter would have been, eligible to vote before leaving the United States is within the Commonwealth of Kentucky; and

   2. The voter has not previously registered to vote in any other state

Registering to Vote (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Military-or-Overseas-Voters.aspx#Registering-to-Vote)

All military and overseas voters must be registered to vote in order to obtain a ballot. UOCAVA voters can register by completing a Federal Post Card Application (FPCA) (https://kentucky.enhancedballot.com/kentucky). The completed FPCA must then be received by the County Clerk’s office on or before the registration deadline for the upcoming election to be added to the voter rolls. Visit Homepage (https://elect.ky.gov) to view registration deadlines.

Request an Absentee Ballot (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Military-or-Overseas-Voters.aspx#Request-an-Absentee-Ballot)

Current registered voters may request an absentee ballot by completing a Federal Post Card Application (FPCA) (https://kentucky.enhancedballot.com/kentucky). The FPCA must be returned to their County Clerk’s office no later than seven (7) days prior to an election.

Receiving an Absentee Ballot (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Military-or-Overseas-Voters.aspx#Receiving-an-Absentee-Ballot)

Tracking Your Ballot (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Military-or-Overseas-Voters.aspx#Tracking-Your-Ballot)

Use our Voter Information Center (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/vic/) to find out when your ballot was sent and if it was received.

Voted Ballots (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Military-or-Overseas-Voters.aspx#Voted-Ballots)

Voted ballots must be received by the County Clerk’s office by the close of polls on election day.

 Visit Homepage (https://elect.ky.gov) for election dates

questions.q: Does Kentucky allow ballot curing?
questions.a: Yes, Kentucky allows voters to fix an issue with their ballot.

questions.q: How will I know if there’s an issue with my absentee or mail-in ballot?
questions.a: If there is a signature mismatch between your signature of record and your ballot, your county election officials will make a reasonable effort to contact you and provide notice to the voter with a timeframe and instructions on how to cure the signature issue.

questions.q: What is the deadline to cure my ballot?
questions.a: The deadline to cure (correct) your absentee/mail ballot is by the close of polls (6pm) on Election Day.

questions.q: Can I track my absentee ballot?
questions.a: You can track the status of your absentee/mail ballot using your state’s online tool (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/VIC/).

questions.q: What is a ballot drop box?
questions.a: A drop box is a secure, locked structure operated by election officials where voters can deliver their absentee ballot any time, day or night.

questions.q: Are drop boxes available in my state?
questions.a: Yes, drop boxes are available in Kentucky.

questions.q: Where can I find ballot drop box locations?
questions.a: There is at least one drop-box per county. You can find your drop box location here (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Polling-Locations.aspx) or contact your local Elections Official. (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

questions.q: Can I track the ballot after placing in the drop box?
questions.a:
No, you can not track your ballot after placing in the drop box.

  Find Drop Box Location  (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Polling-Locations.aspx)

questions.q: Can I vote before Election Day in Kentucky?
questions.a: Yes. Kentucky offers early in-person voting before Election Day.

questions.q: Who can vote early in Kentucky?
questions.a:
Kentucky offers two types of early in-person voting: regular (no-excuse) early voting and excused in-person absentee voting.

Regular Early Voting (No-Excuse In-Person Absentee)

All registered Kentucky voters who have not requested a mail-in absentee ballot may vote early in person without providing a reason.

When: The Thursday, Friday, and Saturday before Election Day. Polls must be open at least eight hours each day between 6 a.m. and 8 p.m. Exact hours are set by the county board of elections.

Where: Your county clerk’s office or another location designated by your county board of elections.

Excused In-Person Absentee Voting

Some registered Kentucky voters may vote earlier if they qualify for an approved excuse and cannot vote during the regular early voting period or on Election Day.

When: The six business days before the regular early voting period, during normal business hours.

Where: Your county clerk’s office or another location designated by your county board of elections. Contact your county board of elections for details.

You may qualify for excused in-person absentee voting if you:

- Will be out of your county on Election Day and during regular early voting
- Have surgery (or your spouse has surgery) requiring hospitalization during early voting and on Election Day
- Temporarily live outside Kentucky but remain eligible to vote in the state
- Are a uniformed-service voter confined to a military base during early voting and on Election Day
- Are in the last trimester of pregnancy
- Are unable to appear at the polls due to age, disability, or illness
- Are scheduled to work all hours the polls are open, including commute time
- Are an election officer working during the election cycle

  Find Early Voting Times and Locations  (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Polling-Locations.aspx)

questions.q: Who is eligible to vote in Kentucky?
questions.a:
To register to vote in Kentucky, you must:

- Be a U.S. citizen and a Kentucky resident for at least 28 days before the election
- Be at least 18 years old by the next General Election

  - Kentucky law allows qualified 17-year-olds to participate in a Primary Election if they will be 18 years old by the General Election
- Not be convicted of a felony (or, if so, have had your civil rights restored)
- Not judged mentally incompetent in a court of law
- Not claiming the right to vote anywhere outside Kentucky

questions.q: Can I vote in Kentucky if I have a felony conviction?
questions.a:
In Kentucky, a felony conviction can take away your right to vote unless your rights have been restored. A misdemeanor conviction does not take away your voting rights. However, you cannot vote if you are incarcerated at the time of the election. If you were convicted of a Kentucky state non-violent felony, your voting rights are automatically restored after you complete your full sentence, including incarceration, parole, and probation. If you were convicted of a violent felony, a federal felony, or a felony in another state, your rights are not automatically restored. You may petition the governor to have your rights restored after completing your sentence and meeting state requirements.

 You can check your status here. (https://secure.kentucky.gov/Corrections/VoterEligibility/search)

  Find Out if your are Eligible to Vote  (https://civilrightsrestoration.ky.gov/Pages/qualify.aspx)

questions.q: Do I need an ID to register to vote in Kentucky?
questions.a: If you register to vote online you may use a current Kentucky driver's license to help you complete the application. No ID is required for in person or mailed applications.

questions.q: What if I don’t have an ID?
questions.a:
The state will make you a free ID card. You get it where you can get a driver’s license, and drive.ky.gov (https://drive.ky.gov/Pages/Find-An-Office.aspx) is where you can find the nearest state office for that.

Voters can call or text 844-338-8743 at any time to reach VoteRiders Voter ID Helpline

questions.q: When are official election results available in Kentucky?
questions.a: Official results are never available on Election Day. Election officials are working around the clock to count a large number of ballots, and it’s essential that they take the time to make sure every vote is counted.

questions.q: Where can I find official election results?
questions.a:
The earliest official election results for the state of Kentucky will be posted here (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/liveresults/). A record of past election results can be found here (https://elect.ky.gov/results/Pages/default.aspx).

  Official Results  (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/liveresults/)

questions.q: What does a poll worker do in Kentucky?
questions.a:
Poll workers in Kentucky, called precinct election officers, help ensure voting is fair, orderly, and accessible on Election Day. Their duties include:

- Attending required training before the election
- Arriving early to set up the polling place with election materials and equipment
- Checking in voters and assisting them as needed
- Following election laws and procedures at the polling place
- Protecting voter privacy and election security
- Closing the polls and returning ballots and materials to the county clerk’s office

questions.q: What qualifications do I need to be a poll worker in Kentucky?
questions.a:
To serve as a precinct election officer in Kentucky, you must:

- Be a registered voter in Kentucky
- Be 18 by the next General Election
- Not be a candidate in the election year
- Not be the spouse, parent, sibling, or child of a candidate on the ballot in your precinct. You may serve in a different precinct
- Not have changed your party affiliation after the deadline for the upcoming election

Training is required before each election. Poll workers must attend training sessions provided by the county to learn election procedures, voting equipment use, and legal requirements.

questions.q: Are poll workers paid in Kentucky?
questions.a: Yes. Precinct election officers are paid for their service. State law provides minimum payments for both training and Election Day work. Some counties may offer additional compensation. Contact your county clerk (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) for specific pay rates.

questions.q: How do I apply to be a poll worker in Kentucky?
questions.a:
You can apply by completing the Precinct Election Officer application (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/ovrweb/pollworker/) on the Kentucky State Board of Elections website. Your information will be sent to your county clerk, who will contact you about serving.

You may also contact your county clerk (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) directly for information about applications, training, and upcoming elections.

  Become a Poll Worker  (https://www.powerthepolls.org/LWV)

questions.q: What is a provisional ballot?
questions.a: Provisional ballots ensure that all voters can cast a ballot even if voter eligibility isn’t certain when they vote. Voters can mark a provisional ballot, and election workers set it aside until eligibility is verified at a later time.

questions.q: Does Kentucky offer provisional voting?
questions.a: Yes, Kentucky offers provisional voting.

questions.q: How do I vote a provisional ballot?
questions.a:
You can vote on federal offices on a provisional ballot if you live in the precinct and you find yourself under one of the approved circumstances. Those circumstances are:

- Your name does not appear on the precinct roster, and the registration status cannot be determined by the precinct officer.
- Your name does not appear on the precinct roster, and you have been verified as ineligible to vote.
- You do not have identification.
- You are voting as a result of a federal or state court order or any order under state law in effect 10 days prior to Election Day which extends polling hours.
- You have been challenged by all four precinct election officers.

questions.q: When are provisional ballots counted?
questions.a: Provisional ballots are counted by 12pm the Friday after the election.

questions.q: How can I check the status of my provisional ballot?
questions.a: To find out if your vote was counted, please go to the Kentucky State Board of Elections’ Provisional Voter Information page. (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/provweb/)

questions.q: What voting assistance is available for voters with disabilities?
questions.a:
The Help America Vote Act requires that election authorities have voting equipment for voters with disabilities to vote privately and independently, and Kentucky is no exception.

For more information on the provisions available for disabled voters, please contact your local election authority (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

questions.q: How do I request accommodation or report accessibility issues?
questions.a: If you have any questions about receiving help in voting, please ask the clerk or inspector at the polling place.

questions.q: Can I vote by mail because of my disability?
questions.a:
If you are unable to go to the polls due to your age, disability, or illness you may vote by absentee ballot.

For more information, you can utilize the American Association of People With Disabilities (AAPD) (http://www.aapd.com/what-we-do/voting/) resource.

  Voting Options for Voters with Disabilities  (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Voters-with-Disabilities.aspx)

questions.q: What do I need to register to vote in Kentucky?
questions.a:
Here is what you need to know to register in Kentucky:

You can register to vote in Kentucky online (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/ovrweb/), by mailing a completed voter registration form (https://elect.ky.gov/Resources/Documents/SBE%2001%20-%20KY%20Voter%20Registration%20Application%20FILLABLE%20406.pdf), or in person (https://elect.ky.gov/About-Us/Pages/County-Clerks.aspx) at your county clerk’s office.

questions.q: Can I register to vote using my college address in Kentucky?
questions.a: Yes, if you consider your campus address your residence, you can register to vote there. If you move to a different dorm or off campus, be sure to update your voter registration with your new address so you vote in the correct district.

questions.q: What’s the deadline to register to vote in Kentucky?
questions.a: The deadline to register to vote in Kentucky is 29 days before Election Day, whether you register online, by mail (postmarked), or in person. Be sure to check the exact date each year.

questions.q: What form of ID do I need to vote in Kentucky?
questions.a: To vote in Kentucky, you must present a photo ID that shows your name and photograph. Some of the accepted IDs include a Kentucky driver’s license, U.S. passport, military ID, college ID, or a government-issued ID from the state or a local Kentucky agency.

questions.q: I’m originally from another state—can I still vote in my home state while studying in Kentucky?
questions.a: Yes, you can vote in your home state using an absentee ballot, but you'll need to follow your home state's rules and deadlines. You can find the rules for your state on VOTE411 or by contacting your state’s election office (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm?_ga=2.80770708.201004602.1748545947-889989650.1701105430).

questions.q: Does registering to vote affect my financial aid, parents’ taxes, and/or tuition in Kentucky?
questions.a: Registering to vote in your college community will not affect your Federal Financial Aid, status as a dependent on your parents’ taxes, or tuition status.

questions.q: Does Kentucky require employers to give time off to vote?
questions.a:
Yes. Kentucky law requires employers to allow employees at least four hours of time off to vote on Election Day, if the employee requests it with advance notice. The employer may choose the hours during which the employee may be absent to vote. Employers are not required to provide paid time off unless company policy states otherwise.

  Learn More  (https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=27563)

questions.q: Do I need ID to vote in Kentucky?
questions.a: Yes. Kentucky requires voters to present a photo ID when voting in person. You must show ID at your polling place or early voting site before casting a ballot.

questions.q: What types of ID can I use to vote in Kentucky?
questions.a:
You have three ways to meet Kentucky’s voter ID requirement:

Option 1: Show a Photo ID

You can vote by showing a photo ID that includes your name and is issued by one of the following:

- Kentucky State Government
- U.S. Federal Government
- U.S. Military, Merchant Marines, or KY National Guard
- A U.S. college or university (public or private)
- A city or county government in Kentucky

The KY Board of Elections offers a short video (https://youtu.be/jxPf-3AujM0) summarizing accepted Voter ID options.

Option 2: Complete a Voter Affirmation Form

If you do not have an acceptable photo ID, you may complete a voter affirmation form at the polls explaining why you cannot obtain one. You must also present one of the following:

- Social Security card
- Any other type of photo ID with your name
- Kentucky food stamp, EBT, or SNAP card with your name

Option 3: Be known by the Election Officer

If a precinct election officer personally knows you and can confirm your identity and residence, they may complete a verification form. In that case, you do not need to show ID.

questions.q: What if I don’t have an acceptable ID?
questions.a:
Kentucky offers a free state-issued ID card for voting purposes. You can obtain a free ID at a Driver Licensing Regional Office. To find the nearest office and learn more, visit drive.ky.gov (https://drive.ky.gov).

If you do not have an acceptable photo ID when you go to vote, you can complete a voter affirmation form at the polling place explaining why you are unable to obtain one. You must also provide an approved supporting document that shows your name, such as a Social Security card, another photo ID with your name, or a Kentucky SNAP, EBT, or food stamp card.

If a precinct election officer personally knows you and can confirm your identity and residence, they may complete a verification form so you can vote without presenting ID.

Do not leave without voting. Poll workers can help you complete the required steps so you can cast your ballot.

questions.q: Does absentee voting in Kentucky require ID?
questions.a:
To request an absentee ballot, most eligible voters must use Kentucky’s online absentee ballot portal. You will need to provide your Social Security number to submit your request.

If you are voting absentee in-person (https://www.vote411.org/kentucky#absentee-ballot-process), you must present a photo ID that includes your name and is issued by one of the following:

- Kentucky State Government
- U.S. Federal Government
- U.S. Military, Merchant Marines, or KY National Guard
- A U.S. college or university (public or private)
- A city or county government in Kentucky

questions.q: Are student or digital IDs accepted to vote in Kentucky?
questions.a:
Yes. A valid student photo ID issued by a Kentucky college or university is accepted as identification when voting in person.

Kentucky law does not specifically address digital IDs for voting. If you plan to use a digital version of your ID at the polls, contact your county clerk (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) before Election Day to confirm whether it will be accepted.

Voters can call or text 844-338-8743 at any time to reach VoteRiders Voter ID Helpline

Contact your state Board of Elections or local Elections Official (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) for more information.

  Voter ID Requirements  (https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Absentee-Excused-In-Person.aspx)

questions.q: What is the deadline to register to vote in Kentucky?
questions.a:
- Online registration deadline: 29 days before Election Day
- Register by mail deadline: Postmarked 29 days before Election Day
- In-person registration deadline: 29 days before Election Day

questions.q: How can I register to vote in Kentucky?
questions.a:
You have several options to register to vote or update your voter registration.

- Online: Visit GoVote.Ky.gov (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/ovrweb/govoteky) to register to vote or update your current registration!
- Mail: Download, print, and complete (https://elect.ky.gov/Resources/Documents/SBE%2001%20-%20KY%20Voter%20Registration%20Application%20FILLABLE%20406.pdf) a paper form and mail it to the State Board of Elections or your county clerk.

questions.q: How can I check my voter registration status?
questions.a: You can verify your voter registration status using Kentucky’s voter information tool. (https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/VIC/)

questions.q: Does Kentucky have online voter registration?
questions.a: Yes! Use our online registration tool (https://www.vote411.org/register) to complete your application

questions.q: Is same-day voter registration available in Kentucky?
questions.a: No, Kentucky does not have same-day voter registration.

questions.q: Can I pre-register to vote?
questions.a:
Yes, you can pre-register to vote if you’re at least 17 years of age.

To vote, you must be at least 17 years old by the Primary Election if you’ll be 18 years old by the General Election.

questions.q: Who is eligible to register in Kentucky?
questions.a:
Check if you’re eligible to register here (https://www.vote411.org/kentucky#eligibility-requirements).

questions.q: What types of voting machines does Kentucky use?
questions.a: The voting systems used in Kentucky are Optical Scan and DRE.

questions.q: What is optical scan voting?
questions.a:
With optical scan voting, you will receive a card or sheet of paper, which you take over to a private table or booth. The card has the names of the various candidates and ballot measures printed on it.

- With a pen or pencil, you fill in a little box, circle, or space between two arrows.
- When you are finished filling out all the cards, you may bring the cards over to a ballot box, where poll workers will show you how to put the cards in the box.
- Or in some places, you may feed the completed cards or papers into a computer device that checks your card or paper right there at the polling place to make sure you have voted the way you want to and counts the votes.

questions.q: What is Direct Recording Electronic Voting?
questions.a:
Direct Recording Electronic (DRE) is the newest system in use in the U.S. All the information about who and what you are voting for is on an electronic screen like a TV or computer screen.

There are many variations of DREs because many companies are inventing new ones, and many cities, counties, and states are trying them out.

- Usually, after you have signed in, the poll workers will give you a card that you slide into a device to start your voting session.
- Some of these devices will show all candidates and ballot choices on one big screen. Often, with these big screen devices you push a button next to the name of the candidate you want to vote for (or yes or no on a ballot measure).
- On other DREs, the screen is set up to show pages. There will probably be one thing on which to vote on each screen or page. For example, on one screen or page, you might vote for the president. Then you might move to the next page to vote for a senator. Often these small-screen devices have a touch screen, where you touch the screen next to the name of the person you want to vote for.
- Other devices have a keypad, and some have a keyboard, so you can write in the name of someone you want to vote for.
- You let the system know you are finished voting by pushing a button, touching the screen or entering something on a keypad.

You can learn more about voting systems by checking out the Elections Assistance Commission's (EAC) resource.  (https://www.eac.gov/voting-equipment/system-certification-process)
